findings.description: The bucket has no default server-side encryption configuration, so objects uploaded without an explicit encryption request may be stored without bucket-enforced encryption.
The bucket has no default server-side encryption configuration. Its private ACL does not ensure that stored ledger exports are encrypted at rest.
The bucket does not define default server-side encryption. Versioning and access logging do not protect model artifacts from being stored unencrypted.
The bucket lacks a default server-side encryption configuration, allowing objects to be uploaded without bucket-enforced encryption at rest.

Although the bucket has default SSE-KMS encryption, its S3 server access logging destination configuration does not enable Bucket Keys or establish a compatible delivery mechanism for SSE-KMS; however, this configuration itself does not substantiate an encryption bypass or public exposure.
